# NHI Security Vendor Landscape (May 2026): Capabilities, Gaps, and Cisco/Astrix Acquisition

Six purpose-built NHI security vendors as of May 2026:

**Astrix Security** (acquired by Cisco, May 2026 — Fortune Cyber 60): Most comprehensive platform. Four-method discovery: direct AI platform integrations (Copilot, Bedrock, Vertex, OpenAI, Agentforce), NHI fingerprinting via OAuth/service accounts, EDR telemetry (CrowdStrike/SentinelOne/Defender), BYOS for homegrown infra. Agent Control Plane (ACP): real-time allow/flag/block policy by user/dept/agent/resource. Threat Center with enriched detections.

**Entro Security**: SDLC-focused scanning across code, CI/CD, cloud, vaults, SaaS. Differentiator: NHIDR (Non-Human Identity Detection & Response) — monitors NHI *activity* for anomalies, not just inventories.

**Oasis Security**: Strongest on hybrid environments. AuthPrint technology fingerprints threat actors at authentication stage against a threat database — reduces false positives by up to 90%.

**Clutch Security**: Fabric model — normalizes NHI attributes (ownership, privileges, secret status, risk score) across AWS/Azure/GCP/SaaS into a unified inventory.

**GitGuardian** ($50M Series C, Feb 2026): Secrets-detection origin. Caught 350,000 secret exposures in 2025. Building full NHI lifecycle management. Best-in-class at finding exposed credentials in code/pipelines; weaker on runtime agent governance.

**Aembit**: Secretless workload auth — Edge sidecar proxy intercepts requests, verifies workload identity via cryptographic attestation, issues short-lived ephemeral tokens. No secret issued = no secret to steal.

**Coverage gap across all vendors**: Runtime per-agent behavioral baselining, agent-to-agent mutual auth, policy governance at agent deployment speed. 68% of orgs cannot distinguish AI agent activity from human activity (CSA/Aembit). Cisco/Astrix acquisition creates displacement demand for independent alternatives.
